maria (devex): FYI the publish pipeline flaked on the post-publish check — CI says typegen produced a diff against the checked-in types.
sudeep: ugh, which package? saw flaky CI earlier on canary.
maria (devex): @sudeep it failed on packages/sdk-node — release job created v1.14.0 but the typegen output changed. attach log below.
ci-bot: [CI] job #4821 failed: postpublish/typegen-check
maria (devex): ```
> yarn workspace @redwood/sdk-node typegen:check
Typegen mismatch: src/types/openapi.d.ts
  - old: export type ApiFoo = { bar?: string }
  + new: export type ApiFoo = { bar: string }
Run `yarn typegen:regen` to update.
``` 
jamie: hmm sounds like a semver mismatch — maybe the generator bumped strictness in a minor release but we tagged minor? did release script bump patch only?
sudeep: release script should run `typegen:regen` before commit if codegen changed, but our CI only runs it on PRs, not on the release branch.
lexi-docs: I noticed the changelog generator also reads the openapi schema version. If the spec had a required flag added, that would change types.
maria (devex): The weird part is the changelog entry included a note about "client types tightening" in the changelog for v1.14.0, but the checked-in types weren't updated in the commit that created the tag.
jamie: Can we abort the publish and republish a patched release? Or do a hotfix commit with typegen regen.
sudeep: Best short fix: revert the tag, push a commit that runs `yarn typegen:regen && git commit -am "chore(sdk-node): regen types" && git push`, then run release again. Non-blocking: we should add a guard in the release workflow to run typegen and fail if there are unstaged changes.
maria (devex): Agreed. I'll do the hotfix now. Going to run locally and open a tiny PR.
regen-bot: Running automated typegen for @redwood/sdk-node...
regen-bot: Produced diff in src/types/openapi.d.ts (1 file)
maria (devex): pushed the regen commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/commit/abcd1234
maria (devex): Created PR #987 with the regen commit and linked to release job
ci-bot: [CI] PR #987: typecheck ✅, unit tests ✅, typegen-check failed (expected — diff present in PR)
jamie: CI failing on typegen-check in the PR is actually good: ensures regen commit is explicit.
lexi-docs: Follow-up: we should document in the release playbook that typegen must be run and committed before tagging. Also add a step to the release GH Action to run `yarn typegen:check` and fail the job if it reports diffs.
sudeep: We should also pin Typegen tooling version in the release container. There was a bump to 2.1.0 that tightened option defaults.
maria (devex): Agreed. I'll open a second PR to the release workflow to run typegen and fail fast. For now, I'll wait for CI on #987 and then re-run the release once merged.
jamie: If we want to avoid future surprises, add an automated step that runs `git status --porcelain` after running typegen in the release action and prints a diff if non-empty.
lexi-docs: I'll update the docs/playbook with the minimal commands and the expected order: 1) regen types 2) run changelog generator 3) commit and tag.
maria (devex): Thanks all — small process fixes should stop this from happening on production publishes. :thumbsup:
sudeep: one more thing: can we add a lint rule to catch changed generated files in PRs? maybe a pre-commit hook that prevents staging them without a regen marker.
jamie: pre-commit for generated files could be noisy, but a CI check that enforces that generated files are only changed with a commit message prefix like "chore(gen): regen" might work.
maria (devex): ok I'm going to merge #987 when CI is green and then bump the release. Will follow up with PRs for workflow + docs.

--end of thread--
